simple.meaning: לַחַץ (lachats) is a Hebrew action word meaning “distress.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 12 times in Exodus, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, and 3 more, beginning at Exodus 3:9. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, kingship, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לַחַץ (H3906) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: לַחַץ (lachats) / H3906 is traced through Exodus 3:9, Deuteronomy 26:7, 1 Kings 22:27, 2 Kings 13:4 with source-language evidence and verse context.
